CONFIDENCE: 0.37
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong carbonyl Raman band at 1699 cm⁻¹ (aromatic aldehyde C=O) together with an intense ring C=C band at 1600 cm⁻¹ and aromatic C–H stretches at 3081 cm⁻¹.  
A very strong out-of-plane C–H deformation at 861 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a 1,4-disubstituted benzene ring, i.e. the benzaldehyde carbonyl plus one para substituent.  
Moderate bands at 637 cm⁻¹ and 603 cm⁻¹ fall in the typical aryl C–Cl stretching region, while no strong C–F band near 1100 cm⁻¹ is present, arguing against the fluoro candidates.  
The pattern (C=O 1699, para-ring 861, C–Cl 600–650) fits p-chlorobenzaldehyde, SMILES O=Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1 (candidate 1), and is less compatible with mono- or multi-fluoro derivatives or more heavily substituted rings.
